body: Cast when Stunned and Cast when Damage Taken have no rate for their condition in PoB: the triggered skill is counted as firing at its cooldown, as if you were always stunned or always taking the damage. Cast on Death marks the skill as triggered with no death condition at all. The gem optimizer never picks them.
evidence: CalcTriggers.lua (PoB 2.68.1): 'cast when stunned' returns only the trigger chance and the skill itself as the source, with no stun frequency. concept.py on a self-cast Fireball Elementalist replaced Spell Echo with Cast when Stunned plus Cooldown Recovery in the 6-link.
title: PoB credits condition triggers as if always triggered

body: PoB's misc calculator doesn't drop a socketed jewel's stats the way a full recalculation does, so a probe that deallocates a socket with a jewel in it gives wrong numbers. eval probes refuse it; use apply.
evidence: test-eval.py (phase 3): probe deltas for such removals differed from editing the XML and reloading it.
title: Calculator probes are wrong when a removed node holds a jewel

body: TotalEHP simulates a run of enemy hits against your pools and mitigation. Between hits only gains when hit (life, mana or ES when hit) refill the pools, and recoup is tracked; leech, regeneration and on-kill recovery aren't used. Compare builds that differ there by hand.
evidence: CalcDefence.lua numberOfHitsToDie (PoB 2.68.1): pools refill only through GainWhenHit and tracked recoup; no regeneration, leech or on-kill stats are read inside the loop.
title: PoB's EHP leaves out leech, regen and on-kill recovery

body: A few uncorrupted 20/20 copies of cheap gems are listed at absurd prices and still pass a minimum-listings filter. Ordinary gems are now priced as the cheaper of a max-level listing and a level 1 copy at the quality, levelled by the player.
evidence: Covens: Fireball 20/20 at 2,015 chaos on 3 listings while Fireball 1/20 was 1 chaos on 106 listings.
title: Price-fixed max-level gem listings on poe.ninja

body: poe.ninja lists few awakened or exceptional gems this league, so with a budget an unlisted one counts as unavailable, not cheap. Re-check each league.
evidence: poe.ninja SkillGem overview for Covens: among awakened and exceptional supports only Empower, Enhance and Enlighten had listings.
title: Most awakened gems aren't in the Covens economy

body: rarecost.py prices a crafted rare from its affix tiers. Even after cutting the table to about a third, it stays above what the trade site shows for the same mods, so budgets err on the safe side. Re-calibrate each league with --trade-check.
evidence: Covens trade checks: wand 0.16 vs 0.83 estimated, belt 0.07 vs 0.37, boots 0.05 vs 1.9 (first table); the table was then cut to about a third.
title: The rare-cost estimate runs above trade prices

body: In repair mode the tree minimized the sum of rule shortfalls and ignored damage. A keystone that clears one whole floor won even when it wrecked the build: Chaos Inoculation zeroes a chaos max-hit floor, so a life-scaling Righteous Fire tree took it and kept 3% of the guide's damage. When a floor couldn't be met, every point went to the shortfall: a totem tree skipped Iron Will (3 points, +111% damage). Fixed two ways: the tree no longer chases the max-hit floors that stand on resists (gear fixes those more cheaply), and floors are now weighted against damage (soft above 70% of each floor, weight 2 against log damage) instead of outranking it.
evidence: Phase 7 back-test, uniques-match mode. Righteous Fire guide: shortfalls on the lab's tree were 3.60 with Chaos Inoculation and 3.96 without (floor:ChaosMaximumHitTaken 0.94 -> 0); damage fell from 114k to 78k at that step, final 3% of the guide. Kinetic Fusillade Ballista guide: 1% of guide damage, Iron Will in the missed-nodes list at +111% for 3 points. After weighted floors (2 seeds, uniques + floors): Spiral 2% -> 19%, Kinetic Fusillade 1% -> 6-8%, Penance 10% -> 19%, Ethereal Knives 97% -> 154%, Soulrend Occultist 120% -> 162%; seven of nine runs meet every hard rule.
title: Summed floor shortfalls let one keystone erase a floor

body: Guides keep swap gems in the main 6-link with enabled=false. Counting them as links made the gem optimizer fill 7 gems into a 6-socket body armour. PoB warns ('too many gems') but still calculates every support, so the damage was overstated. The back-test now counts enabled gems only.
evidence: Summon Raging Spirit guide: main group of 7 gems with Melee Splash disabled. Lab result 127% of guide damage with 6 supports; 68% after the fix with 5.
title: Disabled spare gems in a guide's link group aren't links

body: PoB's 'unreserved Mana is negative' and 'unreserved Life is below 1' warnings counted as a flat shortfall of 1, so a node that cut the overdraw from 400 to 100 mana earned nothing and minion or aura builds stayed broken. They're now graded by the overdraw as a share of the pool (plus 0.01), like the attribute and skill-cost rules.
evidence: Phase 7 back-test, 2 seeds after the change: Holy Relic Necromancer uniques-free 128% with the warning -> 166% with no broken rule; Wretched Defiler spectres uniques-match 8% (one support fitted) -> 37% (five).
title: A flat mana-reservation warning gives the optimizers nothing to climb

body: A trade search that finds one or two listings returns one seller's ask. A 1.8-divine-estimate wand came back at 728 divine from a single listing. Trade prices from fewer than 3 listings are now flagged thin and left out of totals, the same minimum poe.ninja prices use.
evidence: Phase 7 back-test trade checks: Convoking Wand (+1 minion, +1 spell, minion damage) 728.7 div from 1 listing; lab gloves estimated 0.8 div priced at 728.7 from 1 listing; a life belt at 46 div from 2.
title: One trade listing isn't a price

body: Where the trade site had at least 3 comparable listings, rarecost's estimate was a median 2.8x the trade price. The sample leaves out strong rares the trade site can't price (nothing comparable listed), so the true bias is smaller. A 10-divine concept budget therefore buys less rare gear than the market would sell. Calibrate the tier and demand costs against trade data before trusting absolute budgets.
evidence: Phase 7 back-test: 61 rares (guide and lab) priced from 3+ listings; model/trade median 2.79, quartiles 1.15 / 2.79 / 4.68; the model was higher on 47.
title: The rare price model runs high on ordinary rares

body: The pipeline is greedy, so the order of steps (gems before or after the tree, gear slot order) changes the result a lot. Run at least two seeds and keep the best before judging a concept.
evidence: Phase 7 back-test, 2 seeds: Soulrend of the Spiral uniques-free 93M vs 539M; Soulrend Occultist budget 80k vs 1.1M; Summon Raging Spirit uniques-free 9.0M vs 28.9M.
title: Greedy runs vary several-fold by order

body: Every optimizer step can only add mana (tree nodes, gear mods); none removes a skill. A design that kept the guide's auras without the guide's reservation gear stayed overdrawn for good. A step after gear now turns off side skills one at a time while reservation is overdrawn, picking the drop the rules rank best, and refunds them. The overdraw shortfall is no longer capped at the pool, or a design several pools short sees no progress from one aura.
evidence: Phase 7 back-test: Righteous Fire 47 mana short in uniques + floors (Flesh and Stone off: fixed, no damage lost); Soulrend Occultist budget 2,928 short of a 1,089 pool, fixed with six auras off (1.50M -> 1.06M damage; 22% of the guide with a broken rule became 5% with none).
title: No step could turn an aura off
